launch.note: The one home of every per-role launch setting. A role's structured fields are the settings; launch.templates is only the wiring each agent's command follows, and the reader in scripts/paths.sh (pp_route, pp_review, pp_argv) fills its placeholders and fails before any launch on a malformed entry. A model is a family name, never a version: Claude Code resolves opus, sonnet, haiku and fable itself, and builder-codex-pass.sh resolves a Codex family to the newest model the account lists. A null effort is omitted from the command, never defaulted. fast renders as Codex service_tier=fast or Claude --settings {"fastMode":true}; false is the default tier, and the Codex review role takes it from set-up's saved answer only. A headless role (headless: true) is one a script runs with codex exec or claude -p. Every pane role is unboxed: the plugin ships no pane box, so launch.paneBox is not set.

orchestrator.note: Orchestration only; never implements. Plans with the owner, launches Builders, merges.

plan-author.note: The plan main asks for before every build: it writes the plan file and nothing else. Main stops once the plan exists; the build starts only on the owner's own go after reading it. The owner may pick another model and effort when asked; this is the default.

plan-author-second.note: The Panel answer's second planner: writes its own plan beside plan-author's, in parallel, for the merge. Where Fable is not available main runs this seat on another Claude model (seat.sh launch --model) and says so.

plan-judge-sol.note: Judge of the Plan + judge and Panel answers: reads the plan or plans and prints its findings; the planner revises once with them. One round, no judging loop. A project set up with no Codex (profile claude) uses plan-judge-claude instead.

plan-judge-astra.note: The Panel answer's second judge, beside plan-judge-sol: reads both plans and prints its findings for the merge. With no Codex, plan-judge-claude takes its place.

plan-judge-claude.note: The plan judge of a project set up with no Codex (profile claude): a read-only Claude pane in place of plan-judge-sol and plan-judge-astra, which main says when it runs it.

builder.note: One pane per batch in its own worktree, with no advisor, a risky batch included (set-up offers none); builds, runs its own Explore subagents (haiku) and review passes (builder-codex-pass.sh, model from roles.codex-reviewer), hands back a branch. Launched by builder-launch.sh.

codex-reviewer.note: The Codex review pass of the Claude+OpenAI profile. Fast mode is not set here: it changes what a run costs, so it is the owner's answer at set-up (codexFast in the project's .claude/commandeck.json, off by default). With a yes the pass preflight needs service_tier = "fast" in the Codex config.

claude-reviewer.note: The review pass of the Claude-only profile: a headless read-only session on a different family than the Builder's, so the review is not the Builder checking itself.

design-coauthor.note: The design check of a batch marked risky: builder-launch.sh --risky opens this pane before the Builder, and it writes the design note the Builder reads first. It writes that note and no code.

audit-auditor.note: scripts/platform-audit/run.sh: one read-only auditor per area of the project's paved-road registry.

audit-verifier.note: scripts/platform-audit/verify.sh: one verifier per area, tries to disprove each auditor finding with read tools only; verify.sh saves its final message as the verdict. Effort omitted.

lean-worker.note: The commandeck:lean-worker subagent (agents/lean-worker.md): edits, runs and tests with no CLAUDE.md, MCP or skills. agent-model-guard.sh fills a dispatch's missing model and effort from here.

lean-checker.note: The commandeck:lean-checker subagent (agents/lean-checker.md): a blind read-only check, one line per criterion. agent-model-guard.sh fills a dispatch's missing model and effort from here.

review-limits.note: Per Codex review. calls: model calls one review session may make. diffLines: added plus deleted lines in main...HEAD, generated files excluded; a bigger unit is split before review.

seat-liveness.note: read-verdict.sh --state: a seat's background command older than this counts as overdue, not busy, so a hung command cannot hold its driver past the stall line.
